checklist.notes: The introduction-and-clarification dialogue uses personal information and alternating turns, so its intended outcome aligns with the A1.1 objectives and allocated concepts.
The final success condition depends on an unspecified listener, so a solo learner cannot complete or verify the culminating outcome as written.
The lesson correctly builds on previously introduced phonemes, listening, speaking, and personal-information context before introducing minimal pairs and spoken interaction.
The contrast, models, card procedure, and role-play instructions are understandable; Tim should be treated as an invented role when it is not the learner’s name.
Two minimal pairs and a three-turn exchange are suitably bounded for 35 minutes.
The perception-production contrast is potentially useful, the lesson avoids stereotyping, and the authoritative request supplies no Vietnamese-specific claim for this contrast.
The perception and dialogue stages lead toward clarification, but the stated final evidence of success cannot be obtained in the self-study mode promised by the system.

findings.description: The culminating criterion says “the listener choice matches your intended word twice,” but the lesson neither supplies a listener nor gives a solo verification protocol. The preceding self-recording activity does not resolve this final dependency, and no acoustic reference is available.
findings.recommendation: Keep the authorized minimal-pair and spoken-interaction scope, but provide two explicit routes: an optional partner protocol and a viable solo route using delayed, mixed-order playback with concealed labels and a recorded answer log. State that Tim is an invented role when appropriate.

methods: Inspected the lesson against its reconstructed, hash-matched M5 teaching payload and confirmed that no external source payload was supplied.
Compared wording and examples across the closed set of all ten revised lessons for suspicious verbatim duplication beyond shared instructional scaffolding.
Reviewed the audit provenance/copyright result and source-scope constraints as machine evidence without treating them as a web-wide originality check.
copyright_originality_check.scope_limitations: Closed-corpus review of the ten supplied lessons plus their exact M5/request/audit context only; no Internet-wide search, external proprietary corpus, legal opinion, or provider receipt was available.

limitations: This is an independent AI pedagogical review for development evidence only; it is not human review, release approval, certification, or publication authorization.
The governing M5 snapshot retains DRAFT taxonomy and OUTLINE_ONLY curriculum records and is limited to the development lane.
No learner trial, classroom observation, or outcome study was performed.
No audio was supplied, so no acoustic, listening-performance, or pronunciation-performance review was performed.
Originality checking was closed-corpus and artifact-bound; no web-wide plagiarism search, external corpus comparison, or legal determination was performed.
Generation provider provenance was not independently established; UNKNOWN is retained rather than inferred.
Generator reasoning, self-assessment, and prior review records were not inspected.
response.sha256 hashes the canonical UTF-8 JSON of the decision, checklist, findings, copyright_originality_check, and limitations captured in this session.
